tier_reason: The v0.25.1 README table (identical since v0.15.0) shows ttf-parser vs FreeType and stb_truetype on AMD 3700X and Apple M1, and the benchmark code is public (benches/outline/outline.cc, Google Benchmark, meson --buildtype release + cargo --release), but no C++ compiler or rustc version and no FreeType version are named, so it stays first-party tier C rather than A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: benches/outline/README.md: cargo build --release for the C API, meson --buildtype release (meson's release optimization level, no debug), C++14 per meson.build; C++ compiler and rustc versions not stated; FreeType is the system freetype2 (meson requires >=2.8), version not stated
corrections.caveats: The performance table was cut from the current README on 2026-08-06 (commit 'docs: cut the stale comparison table and benchmarks from the README'); it survives in tagged READMEs (read from v0.25.1, v0.20.0, v0.17.0 and v0.15.0, all identical), and v0.12.0 carried an earlier x86-only table (glyf 0.915 vs 1.258 ms, CFF 1.365 vs 5.992 ms), so the numbers are several releases old and were never refreshed. The author's own note under the table: 'FreeType is surprisingly slow, so I'm worried that I've messed something up.' FreeType is asked for unscaled outlines only (FT_Load_Glyph with FT_LOAD_NO_SCALE, then FT_Outline_Decompose), which loads the glyph into a glyph slot before decomposing, while ttf-parser streams segments straight to callbacks; both produce the same segment counts, but this is outline extraction, not rasterization or hinting. Benchmark code is public and CPUs are named, but compilers and library versions are not, so this sits just under tier A. Wins on plain glyf are modest (1.3x to 1.55x) and stb_truetype beats ttf-parser on glyf on x86. The current README says the crate is in maintenance mode (bug fixes only, no performance work) and recommends fontations (read-fonts/skrifa) for new projects.

notes: All eight ttf-parser and FreeType numbers and the derived ratios check out against the tagged README. The record is Rust with a C API, so it does not match a C++ language filter. It is a font parser and outliner rather than a shaper, so the category fit is approximate. Metadata confirmed: 793 stars, MIT OR Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-08-06, not archived, not a fork.

tier_reason: perf/result/segment_utf16.md has five-run UNA vs ICU timings for MSVC 19.12 x64/x86, and the harness is public (perf/perf_segment_utf16.h), but no CPU model, flags or ICU version are given and the author calls the harness 'a mess', so it is first-party tier C.

corrections.license: MIT OR Unlicense (LICENSE.md offers a 'Public Domain License' whose text is the Unlicense, or MIT)
corrections.workload: Count UAX #29 word-break and extended-grapheme-cluster boundaries in 50,000 UTF-16 strings. Each string is three copies of the CC BY-SA 1.0 attribution paragraph in English, Latvian, Russian, Bengali, Chinese, Japanese and Korean (perf/perf_segment_utf16.h fill_1). uni-algo una::views::grapheme/word::utf16 with std::distance is compared against an ICU BreakIterator (createCharacterInstance/createWordInstance, US locale) first()/next() loop. Each figure is the total steady_clock time in milliseconds for all 50,000 strings (lower is better), repeated five times.
corrections.claimed_speedup: MSVC 19.12 x64, first of five runs, total ms for 50,000 strings (unit from the harness's std::chrono milliseconds): word breaks 2355.47 (uni-algo) vs 11379.4 (ICU), 4.83x; grapheme breaks 2067.16 vs 5600.95, 2.71x. MSVC 19.12 x86: word breaks 2544.55 vs 13137.1, 5.16x; grapheme breaks 2239.48 vs 6766.44, 3.02x (ratios derived from page data; the five runs agree within about 1%). GCC 7.3 -O3 rows show uni-algo alone (word 1467.2 ms x64, grapheme 1035.15 ms x64) because ICU was not built under MinGW.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: MSVC 19.12 (Visual Studio 2017 15.5.5), x64 and x86, flags not stated; GCC 7.3 x64/x86 '-03' (as written; presumably -O3) rows have the ICU column at 0; ICU version not stated
corrections.caveats: Category fit is weak: the benchmarked task is Unicode text segmentation, a pre-step of text layout, not font shaping or rasterization, and the baseline is ICU rather than HarfBuzz or FreeType. The result file states no units (the harness prints std::chrono milliseconds), no CPU model, no ICU version and no compiler flags for MSVC, and ICU was measured only under MSVC 2017. The results were committed in April 2023 ('Rename perf tests', 'Update perf tests') from a 2018-era toolchain, and the current harness has to be edited by hand (commented-out includes and defines, main5/generate_table) to reproduce them, so which library version produced the numbers is unclear. The ICU path copies each string into an icu::UnicodeString inside the timed loop; that is negligible next to about 228 microseconds per string for ICU word breaks (derived from page data). The author calls the perf tests 'a mess', and the README claims only performance 'at least the same as other implementations'. Only a UTF-16 test exists. The public-domain option carries no patent grant.

notes: The numbers match the result file exactly, and the units and workload are now filled in from the harness source. tier_reason: The README makes only a qualitative claim ('often matches or exceeds the performance of the best CPU rasterizers ... multi-factor speedups' at large sizes) against unnamed CPU rasterizers. No benchmark numbers are in the repo (README, doc/architecture.md, site/index.html), so tier D.

corrections.baseline: Unnamed 'best CPU rasterizers' (README). FreeType, stb_truetype and font-rs are named as comparison points only in the 2017 Pathfinder 1 blog post (pcwalton.github.io), which is blocked here and is known only from a search snippet.
corrections.caveats: Qualitative claim with no named baseline and no numbers in the repo. The only numbers known are in the 2017 Pathfinder 1 blog post (pcwalton.github.io, blocked here; its source repo is not on GitHub), which predates Pathfinder 3; a search snippet calls that FreeType comparison chart dated and says FreeType has improved since. GPU-only (OpenGL 3+/ES 3+/WebGL 2/Metal), so it is not a drop-in replacement for a CPU rasterizer. The README still says 'under heavy development and is incomplete in various areas', and the C bindings are less complete than the Rust API. Commits from 2024 to 2026 are mostly build and SIMD fixes (last 2026-04-23), and the latest tags are preview-3 (2019) and pathfinder_simd-v0.5.4 (2024). Treat as a lead.

notes: Kept at tier D rather than rejected because the project is notable (3.9k stars, Mozilla Servo). It is Rust with C bindings, which does not match a C++ language filter. It is a GPU glyph and vector rasterizer, not a shaper or layout engine, so the category fit is approximate. Metadata confirmed: MIT OR Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-04-23, not archived, not a fork.
